title: Egg Omelet with Dark‑Green Vegetables, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet prepared without added fat and enriched with dark‑green vegetables such as spinach and broccoli is a nutrient‑dense dish. It provides high‑quality protein, B‑vitamins, vitamin K, folate, iron, and antioxidants. Cooking without oil keeps the calorie count low while preserving the health benefits of both eggs and vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most affordable complete protein sources.
Dark‑green leafy vegetables contain chlorophyll, which may support detoxification processes.
Cooking an omelet without fat retains higher levels of lutein and zeaxanthin, carotenoids important for eye health.
Broccoli is rich in glucoraphanin, a compound that supports the immune system.
Traditionally, omelets were cooked with a small amount of butter, but modern guidelines often recommend fat‑free preparation to reduce calories.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs supply all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K and folate
items.content: Spinach and broccoli provide vitamin K for blood clotting and folate for DNA synthesis.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Dark‑green vegetables are sources of lutein, zeaxanthin, and vitamin C, which combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Bone health support
items.content: Eggs and leafy greens contribute vitamin D and calcium, promoting bone mineralization.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: The absence of added fat makes this dish suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with elevated LDL may need to limit yolk intake.

items.title: Oxalates in spinach
items.content: Spinach is high in oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Risk of undercooking
items.content: Insufficiently cooked eggs may harbor Salmonella bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beat the eggs, fold in finely chopped spinach and broccoli, season with salt and pepper. Pour the mixture onto a pre‑heated non‑stick pan with no oil, cook over medium heat, gently lifting the edges until the omelet sets. Serve hot.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The omelet is best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a non‑stick pan without added fat to retain texture.
